title: Voice: two roots, a human behind each — work placed on the machine that has the data, the report flows home

personas.persona: A developer with two machines at home: their main computer and a 'lab machine'. Short messages, doesn't know file paths on the lab machine.
goals: Get an analysis of the sales data that lives on the lab machine: total revenue per region (units x unit_price) and the best month, saved as a markdown report next to the data on the lab machine. You don't know the exact path, only that the data is on the lab machine.
Meanwhile on this home computer: get a tiny python script that prints a greeting for a given name, with pytest tests, in a folder named greet.
Finally ask which region had the most revenue and how much.
script: Ask for the sales analysis first, mentioning it's on the lab machine.
Then ask for the greet script.
Wait for main to come back; ask the final question; finish.

personas.persona: Sam, the lab technician sitting at the lab machine. Practical, a little hurried, short sentences. Knows the sales data is somewhere on this machine but not the exact folder name.
goals: Get a backup copy of the sales data folder on THIS machine, in a folder named sales-backup, and hear how many data rows (not counting the header line) the sales csv has.
Out of curiosity, ask main whether anyone else has work running on this machine right now — accept whatever it says.
script: Start by waiting about a minute (someone at home is using the other computer first).
Then ask for the backup and the row count in one turn.
Wait for the result, ask the curiosity question, then finish.

checks.name: report written on the lab root
analysis ran as a proxy on lab
checks.title: sales|revenue|analy

checks.name: greet tests pass on home
checks.cmd: cd greet && python3 -m pytest -q >/tmp/pytest.$$.out 2>&1 && echo PYTEST-OK || tail -5 /tmp/pytest.$$.out

checks.name: sales-backup made on lab (an exact copy)
checks.cmd: test -f sales-backup/sales_2026.csv && cmp sales/sales_2026.csv sales-backup/sales_2026.csv && echo BACKUP-OK

voice_checks.name: every spoken turn (both people) reached its MAIN
the owner HEARD the top region (south)
both boxes heard their person (mean box WER <= 0.2)
